findings.title: Google Meet fallback crashes when destination calendar is missing
findings.body: The Meet-to-Cal-Video fallback now does `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` after destructuring `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`. If the array is missing or empty, that value is undefined and this throws TypeError before the booking is created. Previously this was optional chaining (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`), so a Meet event with no destination calendar fell back to Daily. Callers in this PR (confirm, Stripe/PayPal webhooks, reminders) explicitly pass `[]` when no calendar is set, so those Meet bookings will 500 instead of being scheduled.

findings.title: Video booking references lose credentialId
findings.body: referencesToCreate now sets `credentialId` only for calendar results and forces `undefined` for every other result. The previous code stored `result.credentialId` for non-calendar results. Video meeting references are therefore saved without the credential that created them. Cancellation only deletes a video meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set and matches a credential, so newly created video meetings will be left running on the provider after the Cal.com booking is cancelled.

findings.title: Location updates persist empty calendar reference ids
findings.body: updateLocation now copies `externalCalendarId` and `credentialId` from the EventResult (`result.externalId` / `result.credentialId`). CalendarManager.updateEvent never sets those fields; it only returns appName, type, success, uid, updatedEvent, and warnings. Previously this path stored `evt.destinationCalendar.externalId` and fell back to `evt.destinationCalendar.credentialId`. Location changes therefore insert booking references with a null calendar id and null credential id (and an empty uid, because update results expose `updatedEvent`, not `createdEvent`). Later cancel/reschedule cannot target the provider event those references were meant to track.

findings.title: Per-host calendar create still targets only the first destination
findings.body: createAllCalendarEvents loops over every destination calendar and calls createEvent with that destination's credential, but it always passes the original event whose destinationCalendar array still contains every host. Lark (createEvent around line 128), Office 365 (around line 75), and CalDAV (around line 161) all take only index 0. Co-host credentials therefore write to the first host's calendar id: the call 403/404s, or CalDAV's filter matches nothing and createEvent still returns success without creating an object. The stored reference externalId is the co-host calendar, so later updates and deletes look in the wrong place. Google create does look up by credentialId, but its organizer attendee email is still taken from index 0 (CalendarService.ts line 122), so the co-host event is created as if the first host were the organizer.

findings.title: Google update/delete fallback never resolves a calendar id
findings.body: updateEvent and deleteEvent only use destinationCalendar when externalCalendarId is falsy, and then they search for a calendar whose externalId equals that same falsy value. That find can never match a real calendar. The old code used `event.destinationCalendar.externalId` in this branch. Legacy bookings that have no externalCalendarId on the reference now call the Google API with an undefined calendarId, so reschedule and cancel fail (delete no longer falls back to primary either). The same mistake is in deleteEvent around line 315.

findings.title: Collective co-host calendars are dropped in common cases
findings.body: destinationCalendar is set to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has one, and the later `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` then no-ops. If the booking owner has no destination calendar but other collective hosts do, none of those hosts get a calendar event. Separately, team calendars are collected only from `users.slice(1)` (around line 990). When the event type itself has a destination calendar, the organizer's personal destination calendar is never added, so the owner host is skipped while other hosts are included. The booking row also connects only `destinationCalendar[0]`, so the persisted booking calendar does not represent the co-hosts either.

findings.title: Recurring collective cancel deletes the wrong events, repeatedly
findings.body: The new per-reference loop wraps the old recurring-cancel block unchanged. For each calendar reference, that block ignores the reference just fetched and instead walks every calendar credential on the booking owner, and for each remaining occurrence deletes only the first `_calendar` reference (`find`, not `filter`). Co-host events, whose credentials were loaded from the DB on the non-recurring path, are never deleted. The same delete promises are awaited inside the loop and pushed onto apiDeletes, which is awaited again later, so each remaining occurrence is deleted once per calendar reference and then a second time. A two-host recurring series will error or no-op on the other hosts' calendars and hammer the owner's calendar.

findings.title: One missing calendar credential fails every calendar update
findings.body: In updateAllCalendarEvents, if a reference has a credentialId that is neither on the EventManager user nor returned with an app slug, `credential` stays undefined and `updateEvent(undefined, ...)` is still pushed. That rejection fails Promise.all, and the catch now returns every calendar reference as failed without logging (the `console.error(message)` call was removed, and `message` is unused). One co-host credential that cannot be loaded therefore aborts updates for hosts whose calendar calls were valid, and the failure is invisible in logs. The create path correctly skips a missing credential; the update path should do the same.

findings.title: Seat merge deletes only the first host calendar event
findings.body: When newBookingId is set, the code still does `booking.references.find(...)` and deletes that single calendar event. This PR now stores one calendar reference per collective host, but this merge path was not updated to iterate them. Rescheduling into an existing seated booking removes only the first host's old provider event and leaves the other hosts' events on their calendars.

findings.title: Paid confirmation still creates only the owner's calendar event
findings.body: Stripe payment success builds destinationCalendar from the booking calendar or the booking user's calendar only, then calls eventManager.create(evt). Collective co-host calendars are never loaded. Paid bookings do not create provider events in handleNewBooking; they are created here, so the collective-host fix does not apply and co-hosts still get no calendar event after payment. The same single-calendar construction is in paypal-webhook.ts around line 152 and in confirm.handler.ts around line 175, which is what requires-confirmation uses before scheduling.

findings.title: Organization slug is stored under the inverted billing flag
findings.body: Unrelated to calendars, the org create payload changed from `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`. Self-hosted installs with billing disabled used to persist the org slug immediately and will now create organizations with no slug, so org URLs and subdomain setup do not work. Cloud installs with billing enabled used to keep the slug only as metadata.requestedSlug until billing completed, and will now claim the real slug on an unverified, unpaid org. The requestedSlug ternary next to it is equivalent to the old expression; only the slug condition was flipped.

findings.title: Webhook destinationCalendar shape is a breaking, inconsistent change
findings.body: CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar changed from a single DestinationCalendar to DestinationCalendar[] | null, and that object is spread into BOOKING_* webhook payloads. Existing subscribers that read destinationCalendar.externalId or .integration will throw or ignore the field. The PR is marked non-breaking, but the e2e update for BOOKING_REJECTED (null -> []) shows the payload changed. It is also inconsistent across events: handleNewBooking still sends null when unset, while confirm/cancel send []. Consumers cannot rely on either an object or an array.

findings.title: Google create falls back to primary and can duplicate events
findings.body: createEvent now chooses the calendar only by `credentialId === credentialId`, and uses "primary" when that find misses. It no longer uses the destination externalId directly. Destination calendars with a null credentialId, and EventManager's no-credentialId branch that calls createEvent once per credential of that integration (EventManager.ts around line 376), therefore write to primary instead of the configured calendar. Each matching Google credential can insert another primary event. The hangout description patch at line 168 uses `selectedCalendar` without the `|| "primary"` fallback, so that follow-up patch is sent with an undefined calendarId whenever the find misses.
